verdict.rationale: Make's first-party help docs say custom webhooks create a URL that external apps or services can call to send any data. That call triggers execution of a scenario (a Make workflow), and incoming requests can either run the scenario immediately or be queued and processed on a schedule. missing for 10: detailed documentation of how the payload is parsed or mapped into the run, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can expose a custom webhook URL that receives external HTTP requests and starts a workflow run with the payload

citations.quote: custom webhooks allow you to create a url to which you can send any data
webhooks create a url that you can call from an external app or service, or from another use webhooks to trigger the execution
If you don't want to run your immediately after a webhook receives data, you can schedule your to process all webhook requests periodically
